entries.title: Feasts and the town's calendar
entries.answer: Every seventh evening the town feasts, and its year has seasonal festivals. You can pay for a feast: Trade, then Services, then Pay for a feast.
more: Every seventh evening the town feasts (food passed round, music, dancing, toasts) and everyone is in a better mood the next day.
Its year has four seasons of a week each, from Founding Day: the May dance round a maypole in spring, the midsummer bonfire, the town fair late in summer, and more.
Pay for tonight's feast yourself ('Pay for a feast', Trade → Services) and the town remembers who paid.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Trade → Services → Pay for a feast
tips: A feast in your name costs ten coins and one for every mouth.
The board, the crier and the gazette announce what's coming.

entries.title: Celebrations: Founding Day, milestones, new ages
entries.answer: Towns celebrate their Founding Day, each new age and each milestone with gatherings and fireworks.
more: A town celebrates its Founding Day each year (tabards out, honey cakes), the evening it comes into a new age (everybody out, fireworks over the heart), and milestones (25, 50 and 100 folk, the first diamond in its stores) with rockets from its stores and a message to players nearby.

entries.title: The town fair and the fashion show
q: how do i enter a contest
entries.answer: Late in summer each town holds a fair: best bread, wool, fish and honey. On fair day, hold your entry and right-click the village board.
more: The best-dressed folk win a rosette at the fashion show.
controls: [Right-click] village board with your entry (fair day)
[U] → Everything you can do → Home → The fair

entries.title: Fireworks
entries.answer: Towns let off fireworks at celebrations. Ask any folk 'Fireworks' (Town, then Records) for the next show.
more: Towns let off fireworks for new ages, milestones, heroes' nights and festivals; a town with a fireworks maker puts on shows.
Ask any folk 'Fireworks' (Town → Records) for the next ones, and ask the fireworks maker for rockets for your elytra ('Elytra rockets', Trade → Shop).
controls: Fireworks maker → Trade → Shop → Elytra rockets

entries.title: The theatre and wonders
entries.answer: A grown town builds a theatre. Buy a ticket from U, then Everything you can do, then the Home tab.
more: Towns also raise wonders (great buildings that rise over days) shown on the Culture and Perks pages.
controls: [U] → Everything you can do → Home → The theatre

entries.title: Buskers and music (and busking yourself)
entries.answer: Musical folk busk in the street for coins, and you can busk too: U, then Everything you can do, then Home.
more: Folk whose pastime is music busk two evenings in three at the well, the gates and the market: real tunes on a note block, folk stopping to listen and dropping coins in the hat.
A Lute (sticks, string, planks) is the musical folk's comfort.
controls: [U] → Everything you can do → Home → Busk

entries.title: Sport: football, kites and draughts
q: can i play football with villagers
entries.answer: Towns of twenty in stone build a football pitch and play matches every rest day. Children fly kites and play draughts.
more: Once a stone-building town has twenty folk it builds a football pitch; every rest day two of the town's ends play a real match with a Leather Football, and there's a league and a cup.
Children fly kites on dry windy afternoons, and draughts are played on a real board at the tavern and in the park.
tips: Put white wool or birch planks in the stores and you'll see the pitch's lines go down.
The camera's 'Show me something happening' finds a match in play.

entries.title: Birthdays and the town bell
entries.answer: Each folk has a birthday: that day the talk screen suggests a Birthday present, which counts extra.
more: The town bell rings for gatherings, weddings and alarms; the News page lists birthdays and the bell.
